scope: Explain the three blockers through existing canonical cases and retained evidence. This is not a fresh reproduction.

case_explanation_checks.key_answer: Access remains valid at the initial refresh deadline in this controlled execution. The frontend explicitly opens Timeout on refresh expiry.

cause_chain.claim: The expiry condition uses access-expired OR refresh-expired.
A timer runs that condition at refresh expiry.
Expired refresh starts automatic logout. Logout clears local credentials after a one-second wait.

presentation_steps: Seed 15-minute access and an original four-hour refresh credential.
Keep the page visible. Every ten minutes, move the mouse once and wait five quiet seconds.
Return access with another fifteen minutes of validity for each successful extension.
Repeat until 23 extensions finish, with no replacement acquisition.
Cross original refresh expiry while installed access remains valid, then advance one second.
case_explanation_checks.intended_result: No expiry-only logout while access remains usable under the recorded active-session intent.
caveats: Four hours is a fixture lifetime, not a verified PROD setting.
This is not every possible activity sequence. The original refresh must remain unreplaced.
Mouse movement must be followed by five quiet seconds. Continuous mouse movement postpones extension.
Server revocation and independent absolute deadlines remain separate conditions.
Do not describe the observed logout as the backend rejecting an otherwise valid access token.

case_explanation_checks.key_answer: A prior-session response can arrive in the same running page after logout. The candidate can retain and reuse that credential.

cause_chain.claim: Refresh responses enter the shared refresh handler without a session-generation check.
The handler stores the response refresh credential.
Acquisition returns early when the stored credential has strictly more than three hours remaining.
A TOKEN_INVALID_EXPIRED response clears local session storage.

presentation_steps: Start session A and hold delivery of its refresh response.
Use the fixture to revoke A on logout and clear local credentials.
Sign in to session B in the same running page without a full reload.
Deliver A's held response, with more than three hours of validity remaining.
Invoke acquisition 25 seconds before session-B access expiry.
At access expiry invoke relogin. Reject stale session-A recovery with HTTP 401 and TOKEN_INVALID_EXPIRED.
case_explanation_checks.intended_result: Recovery uses session-B credentials and preserves session B. This expectation is an inspected review inference.
caveats: The strict more-than-three-hour reuse threshold is necessary for this recorded skip-replacement mechanism.
The revoked-token rejection is modeled fixture behavior, not a newly observed live provider response.
Both revisions can accept a late response after sign-in. The changed replacement rule worsens that existing race.
Without a replacement opportunity, the baseline control also fails.
Do not reduce the rejection condition to arbitrary HTTP 401. The fixture uses the token-invalid marker.
Acquisition and relogin are direct service calls in the retained diagnostic. No complete manual browser flow was freshly reproduced.

case_explanation_checks.key_answer: No stored refresh credential exists when Timeout mounts. Automatic logout begins before the held usable credential arrives.

cause_chain.claim: The mount effect invokes logout when no refresh exists. Its empty dependency list does not reconsider later delivery.
Logout sets loading and isOnLogout before its one-second wait.
The Extend control receives the loading state during automatic logout.

presentation_steps: Start visible Home with fifteen-minute access and no refresh credential.
At 25 seconds before access expiry start scheduled acquisition and hold only response delivery.
Cross access expiry and let Timeout mount with no refresh in the store.
Deliver the usable held response before the one-second automatic logout wait finishes.
Attempt Extend and advance the remaining logout delay.
case_explanation_checks.intended_result: The usable late refresh enables recovery. Successful recovery installs access and closes the prompt.
caveats: Release after Timeout mounts but before logout completes. Later delivery is a different ordering.
The paired common scheduled-acquisition case fails in both revisions.
The hide-specific variant starts acquisition 26 seconds before access expiry and makes the page visible at expiry.
Old hide-specific execution is NOT_RUN in the fresh review. Do not claim paired hide-specific proof.
Clock and service responses are controlled. This does not establish production latency frequency.

limitations: This is a read-only explanation check against existing cases.
No application source, case definition, or production setting changed.
No PROD frequency, real provider revocation behavior, or new reproduction result was established.
Automated checks do not check the complete approved dictionary or grammar rules.
